conventions.convention: Spacetime is a smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian n-manifold, n ≥ 2, with signature (−,+,…,+). Fields are smooth tensor fields; admitted variations come from smooth field families.

The compact spacelike bifurcation surface B is boundaryless. Its binormal has squared norm −2, its area orientation matches the displayed spacetime-volume contraction, and ∇a ξb = κ εab with constant κ > 0. Variations fix ξ and the embedded B; κ in the variation identity is its background value.

Jξ = θ(φ; Lξφ) − ιξ L and Cξ = Jξ − dQξ. Global compatibility of Qξ, Cξ = 0, δCξ = 0, existence of the asymptotic charge limit, and global exactness of its solution-space one-form are explicit assumptions. Boundary chains satisfy ∂CR = SR − B.

R(X,Y)Z = ∇X∇YZ − ∇Y∇XZ − ∇[X,Y]Z and Rabcd = g(R(ec,ed)eb,ea). P is the Riemann-symmetric curvature derivative at fixed metric and matter-jet arguments. Curvature dependence is algebraic, with no covariant derivatives of curvature; antisymmetrization has weight one.

The charge belongs to the canonical covariant integration-by-parts representative class, permitting the stated Lagrangian/potential ambiguities and exact charge additions, but no independent closed-form addition.

Use c = 1 with action normalization, retaining positive ℏ and kB. In n dimensions [G] = L^(n−2)/action. SW has entropy units; identifying it with physical thermodynamic entropy requires a separate assumption.

load_bearing.statement: Stationary Noether data include a covariant first-variation decomposition, a fixed horizon generator and bifurcation surface, a globally compatible Noether potential with vanishing on-shell and admitted linearized residual constraints, and an asymptotic boundary-charge one-form assumed globally exact on the specified solution space.
Under its smooth algebraic-curvature and canonical-representative hypotheses, Qζ = Wᶜζc + Xᶜᵈ∇[cζd] + Y(φ; Lζφ) + dZ, with (Xᶜᵈ)a₃…aₙ = −Pᵃᵇᶜᵈ(εg)aba₃…aₙ; the exact term is absent when n = 2.

For the stated stationary data and canonical representative, every admitted smooth linearized perturbation fixing ξ and B and satisfying δCξ = 0 obeys δ∫B Qξ = (ℏκ/(2πkB)) δSW, where SW = −(2πkB/ℏ)∫B Pᵃᵇᶜᵈεabεcd dAB and κ is the unperturbed surface gravity.

For the stated stationary data, canonical charge, admitted linearized solution and boundary chains, d(δQξ − ιξθ) = 0 and δHξ = limR∫SR(δQξ − ιξθ) = ∫BδQξ = (ℏκ/(2πkB))δSW. The last equality requires the preceding theorem's derivative-free curvature hypothesis. Einstein–Hilbert normalization gives SW = kB AB/(4Gℏ).

published_dependencies.used_for: Defines Lie differentiation through local-flow pullback, including the action on contravariant slots; used for stationarity, tensor-jet naturality, and the pointwise boost argument.
Identifies form Lie differentiation with tensor Lie differentiation; used in the covariant current and ambiguity calculations.
Converts Lie derivatives into exterior derivatives and contractions in the current-closure, ambiguity, and stationary boundary-identity arguments.
Applies to the explicitly finite smooth singular chains CR and to exact-form integrals on closed B. Its positive-degree formulation includes hypersurface chains when n = 2.

concerns.concern: Proof step 3.1 concludes that applying Aᵃ_b∇aζᵇ = ∇a(Aᵃ_bζᵇ) − (∇aAᵃ_b)ζᵇ to the remaining first-order current terms produces an (n−2)-form potential Wᶜζc. A component divergence is an exterior derivative of such a potential only after the requisite antisymmetry is established. The short missing argument is to write the residual current as jᵃ = Aᵃᵇ_c∇bζᶜ + Bᵃ_cζᶜ and use its on-shell closure for arbitrary generator jets to obtain A⁽ᵃᵇ⁾_c = 0 and the remaining coefficient identity. The cited [Iyer–Wald proof](https://arxiv.org/pdf/gr-qc/9403028), Proposition 4.1, equations (54)–(56), invokes a separate charge-construction algorithm for this passage; the local proof should make its own exterior-form construction explicit.

Facts & Assumptions says 'the algebraic-curvature stationary data and C¹ function f in the Example', whereas the Example explicitly assumes f ∈ C∞(J) throughout the admitted spacetime and variation domain. The calculation is valid under the Example's stronger hypothesis, but this summary should retain that smoothness requirement.
